need: A commit check that fails when a plan changing a requirement does not say, in one line, whether it is small (the proposal is the plan and the planning checklist is not run) or full (it has a planning package), and that prints and counts the sizes declared.

searched.where: scripts/ship.py in this repository (SMALL_PLAN, FENCE, outside_fences, one_page_plan_gaps, one_page_plan_refusal), read 2026-11-18
searched.query: what already reads a declared plan size
searched.found: ship reads the line `Plan size: small` outside fenced code blocks in Markdown pages under docs/plans/ that a merge adds or changes, and refuses the merge when such a page lacks its five headed parts, is over 150 lines or has no recorded independent read. It reads no OpenSpec change and knows no value `full`.

searched.where: company-planning plugins/company-planning/scripts/method_conformance/planning_package.py:44 (LINE_RE) and the docstring of method_conformance/cli.py, read 2026-11-18
searched.query: how a full plan points at its planning package
searched.found: Every plan the plan check adopts carries a line `Planning package: <path>` (the path with or without backticks, the label with or without bold); adoption refuses the plan unless the package validator exits 0 on that file. The check reads plan pages, not OpenSpec changes.

searched.where: src/lockstep/checks/changed.py in this repository (ChangePlan, change_set), read 2026-11-18; code2-workspace agents/topics/working-method.md, section "Plan size"; code2-workspace issue 853
searched.query: what already knows which plan names which changed requirement, and what the size rule says
searched.found: The changed check already lists, for each requirement that differs from the base, the plans that name it, and reads `Closes:` and `Wording-only:` lines from an OpenSpec change's proposal.md and from docs/plans pages. The rule defines three sizes and five conditions for small planned work; nothing checks that an OpenSpec change states a size.

searched.where: OpenSpec 1.13.2 as installed: `openspec schema --help`, `openspec validate --help`, `openspec instructions --help`, and the comments in this repository's openspec/config.yaml, read 2026-11-18. The OpenSpec documentation site was not opened.
searched.query: can OpenSpec itself require a line in a proposal or mark a change as needing less process
searched.found: `openspec schema` (which, validate, fork, init; marked experimental) manages workflow schemas, which decide which artifact files a change has. `rules:` in config.yaml are per-artifact rules given as text when an artifact is written (`openspec instructions`). `openspec validate` lists no option that reads those rules.

searched.where: Web search, 2026-11-18, two queries. Pages named in the results: pypi.org/project/pr-risk-scorer; github.com/Comfy-Org/github-workflows pull request 100; givainc.com/blog/itil-change-types; itsm.tools/change-enablement. Result summaries were read, the pages themselves were not opened. Not searched: Danger's documentation.
searched.query: a tool that fails a pull request check when the description lacks a declared risk tier or change size line; ITIL 4 change enablement change types
searched.found: Tools found compute a risk tier or size from the diff and post a label or comment (pr-risk-scorer; the Comfy-Org workflow, whose check run is neutral and cannot fail a pull request). No tool was found that requires an author-declared size. ITIL 4 change enablement, as the secondary pages describe it, has three declared change types (standard: pre-authorised; normal; emergency) and the type sets the approval route.

candidates.name: ship's `Plan size: small` line
candidates.covers: The line itself, the rule that a line inside a fenced code block does not count, and the check of a one-page plan under docs/plans/.
candidates.misses: Reads only docs/plans/ pages at merge time; has no `full` value; does not know which requirement a plan names.
candidates.reason: The same line and the same fence rule are used, so a plan page that ship accepts states its size for this check too. The changed check adds the value `full` and reads the line in an OpenSpec change's proposal.md as well.

candidates.name: Company Planning's `Planning package:` line
candidates.covers: The line a full plan already carries to point at its planning package, in the form the plan check reads.
candidates.misses: The plan check validates the package; it reads plan pages only and is not run by `make check`.
candidates.reason: The same line form is the pointer a plan marked `full` must carry. This check tests only that the file exists; validating the package stays with Company Planning's plan check.

candidates.name: OpenSpec workflow schemas and per-artifact rules
candidates.covers: A project can fork a schema so that a change has other artifact files, and can give the model rules for writing a proposal.
candidates.misses: A schema changes which files a change has, not how much review it got. The rules are instructions for writing; no validate option was found that fails a change for breaking one.
candidates.reason: Neither produces a failing check, and neither knows which requirements a change names against a base revision.

candidates.name: Risk or size computed from the diff (pr-risk-scorer and similar)
candidates.covers: A size or risk tier on every pull request with no work from the author.
candidates.misses: Computed from the diff, not declared; runs as a GitHub Action, and these repositories merge on a local check with no hosted run; does not read plans.
candidates.reason: Brian approved a declared size. Whether a change needs the full planning package depends on things a diff does not show (spend, whether anything goes outward, whether he asked for a full plan).

candidates.name: ITIL 4 change types (standard, normal, emergency)
candidates.covers: The same idea: a declared change type decides how much approval the change goes through.
candidates.misses: A practice described in a framework, not a program to install.
candidates.reason: Nothing to adopt as a tool. It is evidence that a declared size deciding the process is an established practice, which is what option 7A is.
